newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan opposes heavy oversight of conglomerates.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan opposes heavy oversight of conglomerates.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Thursday that the U.S. central bank should tread lightly in supervising financial conglomerates.
"It should be what we used to call Fed 'lite'," Greenspan told the House Banking Committee.
He said that such consolidated supervision should provide general oversight of conglomerates and should not substitute for functional supervision of their specific affiliates.
"We clearly need to have securities regulators look at securities affiliates," he said. "Banking regulators cannot do that."
In his testimony to the committee, Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt argued for a rational system of functional regulation.
If there is to be an umbrella regulator, it cannot be intrusive and at most should just coordinate the flow of information among the functional regulators, he said.
"If we're dealing with an umbrella regulator, in those entities that have mostly securities activities, the SEC should take on that function," Levitt said.
